brief: A PLA forearm rail for an elbow brace: a flat bar 36 mm wide and 16 mm thick, lying flat. One end is a round end 48 mm in diameter centred on the pivot point, with an 8.2 mm hole straight through at the pivot. The bar runs along its centreline from the pivot point to a fully rounded far end whose centre is 175 mm from the pivot point. Two more 8.2 mm through holes sit on the centreline at 125 mm and 155 mm from the pivot point. Seen from above, with the pivot end on the left and the far end on the right, a lug the full 16 mm thick sticks out from the upper long edge: it is 24 mm wide, centred 46 mm from the pivot point along the bar, and ends in a semicircle of radius 12 mm whose centre is 28 mm from the bar's centreline. A 6.4 mm hole goes straight through the lug at that centre. On the top face, a round boss 20 mm in diameter and 6 mm tall stands centred on that hole, and the hole runs through the boss too. On the bottom face, that 6.4 mm hole has an 11.5 mm counterbore 4 mm deep. Its strength is checked outside Forge, so there is no load case.
note: Passed 34 of 34 and the lug was wrong. The designer drew it as a 24 by 22 box, 16 thick, rounded `top_along_y` at `lug_semicircle_radius` -- the brief's 'ends in a semicircle of radius 12 mm' -- and Forge, finding 12 too round for a 16 mm section, clamped it to 8 on the same edges. The lug came out square-ended in plan with its top long edges rounded, the 20 mm boss overhung the rounding, and REQ_LUG_SEMICIRCLE_RADIUS passed on the parameter table. The last look saw it, wrote its fix in words and no patch, and was recorded 'nothing to change'. The document is the run's, its lug as the designer wrote it before Forge's clamp.

requirements.statement: The flat bar shall be 36 mm wide.
The flat bar shall be 16 mm thick.
The lug shall project at the full bar thickness of 16 mm.
The round pivot end shall be 48 mm in diameter, centred on the pivot point.
The pivot hole and the two further centreline holes shall each be 8.2 mm in diameter.
The fully rounded far end's centre shall be 175 mm from the pivot point along the bar centreline.
A centreline through hole shall sit 125 mm from the pivot point.
A centreline through hole shall sit 155 mm from the pivot point.
The lug projecting from the upper long edge shall be 24 mm wide.
The lug shall be centred 46 mm from the pivot point along the bar.
The lug's outer end shall be a semicircle of 12 mm radius.
The lug semicircle's centre shall be 28 mm from the bar's centreline.
The hole through the lug (and the boss above it) shall be 6.4 mm in diameter.
The round boss on the top face shall be 20 mm in diameter.
The round boss on the top face shall stand 6 mm tall.
The counterbore on the bottom face around the lug hole shall be 11.5 mm in diameter.
The counterbore on the bottom face shall be 4 mm deep.
There shall be exactly three 8.2 mm through holes on the bar centreline: the pivot hole and the two further holes.
requirements.rationale: Pivot hole plus the two holes at 125 mm and 155 mm.

requirements.statement: There shall be exactly one 6.4 mm hole through the lug and boss.
requirements.rationale: Single hole shared by lug, boss and bottom counterbore.

requirements.statement: There shall be exactly one round boss on the top face.
requirements.rationale: Brief describes a single boss standing on the lug hole.

requirements.statement: The part shall have 3 open holes of 8.2 mm.
requirements.rationale: The brief sizes and counts these holes.

requirements.statement: The part shall have 1 open hole of 6.4 mm.
requirements.rationale: The brief sizes and counts these holes.

assumptions.statement: The 'fully rounded' far end is a semicircular end with radius equal to half the bar width, i.e. 18 mm, tangent to both long edges.
assumptions.rationale: The brief gives the far end's centre location (175 mm from pivot) but not its radius; a full round blending the 36 mm wide bar is the standard way to realise a 'fully rounded end'.
assumptions.consequence_if_wrong: If a different radius was intended, the bar's overall length and the blend with its long edges would be wrong, though the centreline and hole positions are unaffected.

assumptions.statement: The bar's two long edges, between the pivot end and the far end, run straight and parallel at 36 mm apart, except where the lug projects.
assumptions.rationale: The brief specifies width and the two rounded ends but does not describe the edge profile along the bar's length.
assumptions.consequence_if_wrong: A tapered or curved edge profile would change the bar's planform and the lug's apparent projection.

assumptions.statement: Exposed edges and corners are given a light break/deburr suitable for skin contact, as ordinary good practice for a wearable part, with no specific finish spec called out.
assumptions.rationale: The part is a forearm rail for a brace and will contact or sit near skin, but the brief gives no explicit finish requirement.
assumptions.consequence_if_wrong: Sharp edges could cause discomfort or minor injury against skin if a smoother finish was actually required.

assumptions.statement: All stated hole diameters and positions are nominal, held to ordinary FDM-printing tolerance (approx. ±0.1-0.2 mm), with no tighter fit specified.
assumptions.rationale: The brief gives nominal figures only; no tolerance class is stated.
assumptions.consequence_if_wrong: A tighter tolerance requirement (e.g. for a precision pivot fit) would not be met without secondary machining.

assumptions.statement: The rail operates in ordinary ambient indoor conditions (room temperature, dry), not exposed to significant heat, moisture, or chemical exposure beyond normal wear.
assumptions.rationale: No environmental conditions are stated; PLA is sensitive to heat and moisture over time, relevant for a wearable brace.
assumptions.consequence_if_wrong: Elevated temperature or sustained moisture exposure could degrade PLA mechanical properties, relevant to the externally-checked strength case.

assumptions.statement: The counterbore is coaxial with and perpendicular to the lug hole, with a flat bottom suitable for seating a fastener head, cut from the bottom face.
assumptions.rationale: Standard counterbore construction; the brief specifies diameter and depth but not orientation details.
assumptions.consequence_if_wrong: A misaligned or non-flat counterbore would not properly seat a fastener head.

notes: dropped 1 load question(s): the brief states that this part carries no load, so there was nothing to be uncertain about

added REQ_HOLES_8_2MM: the brief states 3 open holes of 8.2 mm, counted on the built part by diameter. A claim bound to a hole's parameter passes whenever some hole reads that parameter -- a collar had both set screws drawn at the bore's 12 mm, and no bore, and it passed.

added REQ_HOLES_6_4MM: the brief states 1 open hole of 6.4 mm, counted on the built part by diameter. A claim bound to a hole's parameter passes whenever some hole reads that parameter -- a collar had both set screws drawn at the bore's 12 mm, and no bore, and it passed.

document.name: Elbow Brace Forearm Rail
document.description: A flat PLA rail running from a round pivot end to a fully rounded far end, carrying three centreline through-holes, a lugged tab on its upper edge with a bossed secondary pivot/strap hole and bottom counterbore.

parameters.description: Lug stands the full bar thickness
Assumed: far end fully rounded at half the bar width (not stated explicitly, see ASM_FAR_END_RADIUS)
Extent of the lug box from the bar's edge to the tip of its rounded end

features.description: Straight run of the bar from pivot to far end
Lug projecting from the upper long edge, full thickness, rounded tip
Round boss on the top face over the lug hole
Centreline through-hole at 125 mm from pivot
Centreline through-hole at 155 mm from pivot
Through hole shared by lug and boss, with bottom-face counterbore

interfaces.description: Primary pivot connection at the rail's left end
Secondary pivot or strap attachment through the lug and boss
